evals.prompt: This user_report.py came out of an AI coding session and it's drowning in comments and tiny helpers. Can you de-slop it and make it read like a human wrote it? Please write the cleaned file back.
evals.expected_output: Every comment in the file is restatement, narration, banner, or hollow claim, so the cleaned file ends at zero comment lines. The public docstring on generate_report is deleted too -- it is both hollow and a public doc-comment, and nothing in this session authorized one. Emoji removed, single-use helper get_count inlined, x=f();return x collapsed, generic names given meaning where they are not tiny-scope. Behavior preserved. No new comments added; the report states the comment ledger (N lines -> 0).
assertions: Zero comment lines remain (all were restatement/narration/banner)
Public docstring on generate_report deleted, not merely shortened
No emoji remain in the cleaned file
Single-use helper get_count inlined (definition gone)
assign-then-return intermediates collapsed
Behavior preserved on sample input
Report includes a comment ledger showing the count did not increase

evals.prompt: Here's sync_orders.ts that an AI assistant generated. Tighten it up and strip the AI slop before I commit it.
evals.expected_output: Stylistic slop cleaned: the 4-line JSDoc block on the exported function is deleted outright (hollow claims plus a banned public doc-comment with @param/@returns ceremony), banner removed, restating and narrating comments removed, redundant result variable collapsed. No surviving comment run exceeds one line. CRITICAL: the behavioral/security issues are FLAGGED for review, not silently edited or deleted -- hardcoded API_KEY, swallowed catch that leaves data undefined, likely-hallucinated 'sql-secure-builder' import, SQL built by string concatenation (injection). The report separates what was cleaned from what was flagged and states the comment ledger.
assertions: JSDoc block on the exported function removed entirely
No surviving comment run exceeds one line
Banner and hollow/restating comments removed
Hardcoded secret NOT silently deleted (kept in code to be flagged)
SQL injection line preserved, not silently rewritten
Possibly-hallucinated import kept for human verification
Swallowed catch behavior not silently altered
Report flags all four behavioral/security issues (secret, injection, swallow, import)

evals.prompt: Run an anti-slop pass over this payment.go and remove the AI-generated junk, but be careful not to break anything or strip stuff that's actually meaningful.
evals.expected_output: The strict comment policy applied without collateral damage. Deleted: the '// increment retries' restatement, the emoji in the error string, and BOTH two-line doc-comments on exported symbols -- Gateway's (the unit is already carried by the amountCents parameter name, so the comment is restatement) and Pay's first sentence (the signature retyped). The genuine why in Pay's second sentence -- the gateway treats non-positive amounts as full refunds -- is RELOCATED, not lost: it survives as a single line at the amountCents <= 0 guard it explains. Carve-outs left intact: role-suffixed names (StripeClient, CloudPaymentsClient, OrderManager, NewOrderManager), the boundary validation guards, and the Gateway interface with its two implementations. Behavior preserved.
assertions: Real slop removed: '// increment retries' comment gone
Real slop removed: emoji gone from error string
No comment run in the file exceeds one line
No doc-comment remains directly above an exported symbol (Gateway, Pay, NewOrderManager)
The 'full refunds' why is preserved somewhere in the file, not dropped
The 'full refunds' why sits at the guard it explains, not as a doc-header
Carve-out kept: role-suffixed domain names preserved
Carve-out kept: boundary validation preserved (amount + accountID guards)
No over-cleaning: interface + both implementations intact
